title: Jury was ‘inflamed by prejudice,’ SHRM appeal argues
summary: In an opening appeal, SHRM argued that a trial it lost late last year was unfair due to how the jury was directed and its “excessive” award of $11.5 million.

title: Worker alleges lack of fossil fuel-free 401(k) option violated his religious rights
summary: A lawsuit tying a worker’s climate objections to his Christian beliefs could set a precedent in the post-Groff landscape, his attorneys argued.

title: Which skills can AI not replace?
summary: Employers are in need of “durable skills” despite swift changes to workplace technology, a Resume Now report indicated.

title: Class ceiling: What cultural background has to do with salary negotiation
summary: A new study shows that social background factors into workers’ ability to negotiate — or not — and how HR professionals judge them.

title: CHROs say they are skeptical about AI readiness
summary: The executives with the most insight into workforce preparedness are the ones most likely to be cautious about timelines, according to a Protiviti survey.

title: How will AI affect workplace accommodations?
summary: “AI is busting down barriers,” said Julie Hocker, assistant secretary of labor for disability employment policy.

title: After leave, return-to-work approaches should be ‘early, coordinated and sustained,’ DOL official says
summary: The likelihood of an employee returning to work after injury drops off significantly as the weeks go on, Julie Hocker said.

title: Barber school settles claim it wouldn’t employ more than one pregnant worker
summary: Pregnancy discrimination claims have featured heavily in recent EEOC litigation despite ongoing controversy over agency regulations.

title: NLRB’s structure is unconstitutional but its activities may proceed, Texas judge rules
summary: The decision follows up on the U.S. Supreme Court’s recent expansion of presidential power to dismiss leaders of federal agencies.

title: Week in review: How does HR use ChatGPT?
summary: We’re rounding up last week’s stories, including the percentage of executives who said their leaders are prepared to lead AI adoption.
